findings.claim: The Lords cannot delay finance (money) Bills.
findings.truth: The Lords cannot amend Money Bills, but they can delay them for up to one month; most other public Bills can be delayed for about a year.
findings.evidence: UK Parliament, The Parliament Acts (fetched), lines 165–168.

findings.claim: Westminster general elections take place every five years.
findings.truth: They usually take place every five years; an election can take place earlier.
findings.evidence: GOV.UK, Types of election: General election (fetched), line 56.

findings.claim: The Additional Member System is used for Welsh Senedd elections.
findings.truth: From the 2026 Senedd election, Wales uses a closed-list proportional system with the D’Hondt formula; AMS remains used for Scottish Parliament elections.
findings.evidence: GOV.WALES, Senedd reform (fetched), lines 46–56.

findings.claim: English Votes for English Laws is a current constitutional arrangement under which only English MPs may vote on England-only legislation.
findings.truth: EVEL was a House of Commons procedure. Its Standing Orders were rescinded on 13 July 2021, so the procedure no longer applies.
findings.evidence: House of Commons Library, English votes for English laws (fetched), lines 29–34.

findings.claim: A government's mandate comes from winning a clear majority of votes.
findings.truth: In UK parliamentary politics, a government claims its mandate after winning enough Commons seats to form a government; a popular-vote majority is not required.
findings.evidence: Electoral Commission, UK Parliament (fetched), lines 109–114; AQA spec 3.4.3.

findings.claim: The credited argument says that 16-year-olds can marry throughout the UK.
findings.truth: Marriage and civil partnership require an age of 18 in England and Wales. A safe argument is that 16-year-olds can vote in Scottish Parliament and Senedd elections.
findings.evidence: GOV.UK, Marriages and civil partnerships in England and Wales (fetched), lines 53–70; GOV.UK election guidance (fetched), lines 152–161 and 187–197.

findings.claim: A school governor is included in an answer about roles in the justice system.
findings.truth: School governors serve in education, not the justice system. Magistrates, jurors and special constables are relevant examples.
findings.evidence: Recomputation of the answer against the question's scope.

findings.claim: An e-petition with enough signatures triggers a parliamentary debate.
findings.truth: At 100,000 signatures, Parliament considers a petition for debate; a debate is not automatic.
findings.evidence: UK Government and Parliament petitions site (fetched), lines 58–60.

findings.claim: Ninety-seven people died in 1989 and a ninety-eighth victim died in 2021.
findings.truth: There were 97 deaths in total. Ninety-four people died on the day, one shortly afterwards, and two later in 1993 and 2021.
findings.evidence: Hillsborough disaster, Wikipedia (fetched), lines 213–234.

findings.claim: The 2012 Hillsborough Independent Panel report found that 96 victims were unlawfully killed.
findings.truth: The Panel found that no Liverpool fans were responsible, identified failures including altered police statements, and published in 2012. The 2016 inquest jury returned the unlawful-killing verdicts.
findings.evidence: Hillsborough disaster, Wikipedia (fetched), lines 240–241 and 441–467.

findings.claim: 'Nationality of birth country' is the only option presented as not protected by the Equality Act 2010.
findings.truth: Nationality is protected as part of race. Political opinion is not one of the nine protected characteristics.
findings.evidence: Equality Act 2010, Wikipedia (fetched), lines 228–231.
